title: Morocco crowned AFCON winners 57 days after final as Senegal’s victory declared void
content:
The result of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final has been reversed, with Morocco now standing as 3-0 winners after a stunning decision from the competition organisers.

The Confederation of African Football released a statement on Tuesday evening saying that its appeal board had declared that Senegal have now forfeited the game, which they had won 1-0 on January 18.

CAF said the decision came after an appeal from the Royal Moroccan Football Federation following that match, which Senegal won in extra time after walking off the field during normal time in protest at a refereeing decision.

Play was delayed by around 16 minutes after Morocco were awarded a late penalty, after Senegal had seen a potential match-winning goal disallowed, with captain Sadio Mane their only player remaining on the field in Rabat. Following the delay, Morocco’s Brahim Diaz missed his penalty and Senegal’s Pape Gueye scored the game’s only goal in the 94th minute.

CAF’s statement, released 57 days after the final, said that “all other motions or prayers for relief are dismissed” following the decision of its appeals board, which ruled in favour of the Morocco appeal.

At the end of the final, Morocco head coach Walid Regragui, who has since resigned from his role, said of the incident around the penalty gave a “shameful and disgraceful” image of African football. “The coach (Pape Thiaw) asked his players to leave the pitch,” Regragui added. “I have always said that in the end, you must always stay in place in defeat and victory alike.”
